design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 44 patients were randomized to LigaSure or diathermy haemorrhoidectomy using sequentially numbered sealed envelopes with allocations determined before the trial commenced.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation used sequentially numbered sealed envelopes prepared before recruitment and baseline characteristics were broadly balanced, the sequence-generation method, envelope opacity/tamper resistance, and the meaning of “nonconsecutive” randomization were not adequately described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were randomized to receive either LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy or conventional haemorrhoidectomy using sealed envelopes. The randomization performed was nonconsecutive in nature. The envelopes were sequentially numbered with allocations determined before the trial commenced.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients were blinded and perioperative care was standardized, but surgeons necessarily knew treatment assignment and the report does not explicitly describe intervention deviations or an intention-to-treat analysis; one randomized participant was excluded from evaluation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were blinded to the type of surgery performed... A standard medication package was issued to all patients postoperatively... One patient in the LigaSure arm was lost to follow-up, and thus only 21 patients were evaluated in that group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 43 of 44 randomized patients (97.7%), with only one participant lost from the LigaSure group, making material bias from missingness unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomized 44 patients, 22 to LigaSure and 22 to diathermy; 43 patients were evaluated.

domain_judgments.rationale: Several measures were appropriate and standardized, and patients were blinded for self-reported pain, but the primary favorable wound-healing outcome was subjectively graded by a single assessor whose blinding was not reported and who therefore could plausibly have been influenced by knowledge of surgery received.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Wound healing was defined as complete epithelialization as seen on physical examination. The state of the wound was graded according to a five-point scale from sloughy to completely healed... A single assessor performed the assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective protocol or analysis plan is reported, multiple outcomes and repeated time points were assessed, and the trial was stopped at 44 rather than the planned 90 participants for a resource-related reason after which a post-hoc power analysis was used, creating substantial scope for selective analysis or emphasis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although the initially calculated sample size was 90, the study had to be concluded earlier as the supplier of the LigaSure electrodes could not continue to provide the electrodes for the trial without passing on the cost to the patient. However, as the difference in rate of wound healing was high, a post-hoc power analysis revealed a power of 88.8% despite the small sample size.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by possible unblinded subjective assessment of the favorable wound-healing outcome and substantial selective-reporting concerns given multiple outcomes/time points, absence of a reported prespecified analysis plan, early termination below the target sample, and reliance on post-hoc power. Randomization and analysis reporting also leave some concerns, although missing outcome data were minimal.
